questions.q: The editorial says the political empires of the past cannot return. What kind of “empire” does it say is open to any group today?
options: A return to rule by kings
Not quite. The article says: Peaceful, non-political ones – in education, industry, media and ideas.
Peaceful, non-political ones – in education, industry, media and ideas
Yes. This is what the present age makes possible.
A military alliance of nations
Not quite. The article says: Peaceful, non-political ones – in education, industry, media and ideas.
A single world government
Not quite. The article says: Peaceful, non-political ones – in education, industry, media and ideas.
questions.rationale: “Building non-political empires is possible for any group in this age… educational empire, industrial empire, media empire, as well as spiritual and ideological empire.”

questions.q: What does the article give as the deeper purpose of peace of mind?
options: It keeps thinking in a positive direction, which makes intellectual growth and wisdom possible
Right. Only a peaceful mind draws the right lessons.
It helps one sleep soundly
Not quite. The article says: It keeps thinking in a positive direction, which makes intellectual growth and wisdom possible.
It keeps other people at a distance
Not quite. The article says: It keeps thinking in a positive direction, which makes intellectual growth and wisdom possible.
It improves one’s income
Not quite. The article says: It keeps thinking in a positive direction, which makes intellectual growth and wisdom possible.
questions.rationale: “A peaceful mind is another name for a positive mind… Only a peaceful mind will be able to take the right lessons from these sources.”

questions.q: Which three sources of intellectual development does the article name?
options: Rank, title and reputation
Not quite. The article says: Study, observation and discussion.
Study, observation and discussion
Correct. All three work through the mind.
Wealth, travel and leisure
Not quite. The article says: Study, observation and discussion.
Memory, habit and custom
Not quite. The article says: Study, observation and discussion.
questions.rationale: “There are three major sources of intellectual development—study, observation and discussion.”

questions.q: A newspaper begun on a wooden press in 1782 was, two centuries later, printed by laser and computer. What does the article say allowed it to benefit from each new technique?
options: It moved from city to city
Not quite. The article says: It never stopped publishing – enthusiasm and perseverance kept it going.
It never stopped publishing – enthusiasm and perseverance kept it going
Yes. Had it stopped, the techniques would have passed it by.
It had no competitors
Not quite. The article says: It never stopped publishing – enthusiasm and perseverance kept it going.
It was bought by a rich company
Not quite. The article says: It never stopped publishing – enthusiasm and perseverance kept it going.
questions.rationale: “It was only because of its continued publication that it could benefit from all the new improved techniques… great work requires two things in particular: Limitless enthusiasm and perseverance.”

questions.q: The words “Allahu Akbar” – God is great – are repeated throughout the prayer. What does the article say is implied in them?
options: That the mosque is a great building
Not quite. The article says: That the one saying them is not great – a lesson in modesty.
That the one saying them is not great – a lesson in modesty
Yes. It is meant to rid the worshipper of arrogance.
That the prayer is nearly over
Not quite. The article says: That the one saying them is not great – a lesson in modesty.
That the congregation is large
Not quite. The article says: That the one saying them is not great – a lesson in modesty.
questions.rationale: “Implicit in these words is the idea that the person uttering them is not great. Their frequent repetition is a lesson in modesty.”

questions.q: Where, according to the article, does the real proof of a worshipper’s submission to God appear?
options: In his dealings with other people afterwards, in humility and goodwill
Well read. The prayer ends with words of peace to all.
In how often he visits the mosque
Not quite. The article says: In his dealings with other people afterwards, in humility and goodwill.
In the beauty of his recitation
Not quite. The article says: In his dealings with other people afterwards, in humility and goodwill.
In the length of his prostration
Not quite. The article says: In his dealings with other people afterwards, in humility and goodwill.
questions.rationale: “Real proof of this submission to God will only become manifest, however, in subsequent dealings with other human beings.”

questions.q: How does the article advise a community to regard the difficulties it faces from others?
options: As a reason to withdraw from society
Not quite. The article says: As a challenge to be met with right planning, not something to complain about.
As proof that effort is useless
Not quite. The article says: As a challenge to be met with right planning, not something to complain about.
As a plot that cannot be overcome
Not quite. The article says: As a challenge to be met with right planning, not something to complain about.
As a challenge to be met with right planning, not something to complain about
Right. One reaps what one sows.
questions.rationale: “Challenge is not meant to be complained against, but to be faced with right planning… If someone receives less, he should revise his method of work and re-plan.”

questions.q: The discovery of an immense black hole is said to teach two lessons. Which?
options: That the universe has an all-powerful Creator, and that He is merciful in making the earth fit for us
Yes. Together they instil modesty.
That the sun is small, and that space is empty
Not quite. The article says: That the universe has an all-powerful Creator, and that He is merciful in making the earth fit for us.
That science is complete, and that religion is not needed
Not quite. The article says: That the universe has an all-powerful Creator, and that He is merciful in making the earth fit for us.
That the universe is hostile, and that the earth is in danger
Not quite. The article says: That the universe has an all-powerful Creator, and that He is merciful in making the earth fit for us.
questions.rationale: “On the one hand, they strengthen the conviction that this Universe has an all-powerful Creator. On the other hand… this all-powerful Creator is so Merciful.”

questions.q: “A loving heart is the beginning of all knowledge.” What does the article add to make Carlyle’s saying complete?
options: That knowledge must come before love
Not quite. The article says: That it means loving even where there is cause for hatred.
That only family can be truly loved
Not quite. The article says: That it means loving even where there is cause for hatred.
That love must be returned to be real
Not quite. The article says: That it means loving even where there is cause for hatred.
That it means loving even where there is cause for hatred
Exactly. Carlyle himself rose above old prejudice to study the Prophet fairly.
questions.rationale: “Its meaningfulness cannot be properly understood unless these words are added to it, ‘Loving, despite there being a cause for hatred’.”

questions.q: According to the remark quoted from Dale Carnegie, what distinguishes a person of sense?
options: The ability to blame losses on bad luck
Not quite. The article says: The ability to profit from losses.
The ability to avoid all losses
Not quite. The article says: The ability to profit from losses.
The ability to hide losses from others
Not quite. The article says: The ability to profit from losses.
The ability to profit from losses
Yes. Anyone can make use of gains.
questions.rationale: “The really important thing is to profit from your losses. That requires intelligence; and it makes the difference between a man of sense and a fool.”
